document: Instructions for Form PENS.E/2-B - Payment Instructions for Survivors' Benefits
governing_article: Articles 34, 35 bis, 35 ter, 36, 37 of the UNJSPF Regulations

chunks.heading: Purpose of form PENS.E/2-B
chunks.text: If you are a surviving spouse, divorced surviving spouse, spouse married after separation, child, or secondary dependant of a deceased UNJSPF participant or retiree, you may be eligible for a survivors' benefit. Form PENS.E/2-B is used to request payment of that benefit.

chunks.heading: How to notify the Fund of a death
chunks.text: It is important to inform the Fund of a participant's, retiree's, or beneficiary's death as soon as possible. For active participants, the employing organization is responsible for notifying the Fund. For retirees and beneficiaries, the quickest method is emailing unjspf-deathrelated@un.org, or contacting the Fund by phone or the contact form on its website. Communications about a death are given priority by UNJSPF.

chunks.heading: Surviving spouse's benefit (article 34)
chunks.text: Payable to the surviving spouse of a retiree entitled to a retirement, early retirement, deferred retirement, or disability benefit if married to the retiree at separation and remained married until death; or to the surviving spouse of a participant who died in service if married to the participant at the date of death.

chunks.heading: Divorced surviving spouse's benefit (article 35 bis)
chunks.text: Payable if the participant died in service or was entitled to a retirement-type or disability benefit at death; the marriage lasted a continuous period of at least 10 years during which contributions were paid (or the participant received a disability benefit); death occurred within 15 years of the divorce becoming final (unless a legal maintenance obligation existed at death); the former spouse is at least 40 years old; and the divorce settlement did not expressly renounce UNJSPF pension entitlements.

chunks.heading: Spouse married after separation (article 35 ter)
chunks.text: Not eligible for a widow's/widower's benefit unless the retiree or disability-benefit recipient previously elected to provide a periodic benefit for life to that spouse by purchasing an annuity within one year of the marriage (see form PENS.E/3-A).

chunks.heading: Child's benefit (article 36)
chunks.text: Payable to a surviving child under age 21 if the participant died in service; or, if the retiree/beneficiary dies, if the deceased was entitled to a normal retirement, early retirement, or disability benefit and the child is under 21. A disabled child may receive a monthly benefit beyond age 21.

chunks.heading: Secondary dependant's benefit (article 37)
chunks.text: Payable to not more than one surviving secondary dependant (e.g. a parent or sibling) in the case of death of a participant in service or during entitlement to a retirement-type or disability benefit, provided no benefit is or was payable to a child or spouse (including a divorced spouse).

chunks.heading: Section 1 and 2: deceased participant and survivor information
chunks.text: Section 1 requires the deceased participant's/retiree's UID and full name (pension number optional). Section 2 requires the survivor's UID, full name, date of birth, and contact information. UID can be requested via requestUIDonly@unjspf.org.

chunks.heading: Section 3: appointed legal guardian information
chunks.text: Complete this section only if a legal guardian has been appointed - required if a child is unable to manage his or her own financial affairs, per UNJSPF's legal guardianship policy.

chunks.heading: Section 5: bank account information - payee name and account requirements
chunks.text: Payee name must match the bank statement; payment can only be made to an account in the survivor's own name or a joint account also held in their name (not to a third party or by cheque to a mailing address). Monthly benefits are paid into one account only and cannot be split.

chunks.heading: Section 5: currency of payment options
chunks.text: Default currency is USD. Periodic benefit payments may also be paid in AUD, CAD, CHF, CLP, DKK, EUR, GBP, INR, JPY, NOK, NZD, PEN, PKR, RUB, SEK, SGD, XAF, or XOF using the UNJSPF quarterly exchange rate, under the two-track pension adjustment system, regardless of the beneficiary's elected country of residence.

chunks.heading: Banking requirements table - key points
chunks.text: Requirements for account number format, bank ID code (SWIFT, ACH routing number, sort code, IFSC, BSB, NCC, etc.), and intermediary/correspondent bank vary by currency and bank location - e.g. US accounts need a 9-digit ACH routing number; UK accounts need a 6-digit sort code; EUR SEPA/Eurozone accounts need an IBAN plus SWIFT code; accounts outside the specified zones generally need a SWIFT code and an intermediary/correspondent bank.

chunks.heading: Section 6: emergency contact
chunks.text: The emergency contact's details are for UNJSPF's use only when all efforts to reach the beneficiary through normal channels fail.

chunks.heading: Section 7: documents to submit with form PENS.E/2-B
chunks.text: A copy of the participant's death certificate (if not already provided), a valid government-issued photo ID, a recent bank statement/document matching the payment instructions, birth certificates of any children under 21 (and disabled children over 21), a marriage certificate, and any divorce decree(s) for previous marriages.

chunks.heading: Section 8: signature authentication requirement
chunks.text: For UNJSPF to accept the signature as duly authenticated, it must be signed and dated in the presence of an authenticating official (UN official, government official, or notary public), who must complete their printed name, email, official title/licence/index number, original ink signature, authentication date matching the signing date, and official stamp/seal.

chunks.heading: How and where to submit form PENS.E/2-B
chunks.text: In case of death in service, the form goes to the secretary of the deceased staff member's Staff Pension Committee. Otherwise (death after service, or for spouses/children/dependants of UN family staff), it is returned directly to UNJSPF, either via MSS Document Upload or by mail to UNJSPF's New York or Geneva offices.
